Playbook.name: AD/Windows — Audit Policy Changed by Interactive Account - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: The system audit policy was changed (4719) by an interactive (non-machine, non-service) account. The rule already excludes machine/SYSTEM/service accounts, so this is specifically a human-driven audit change. Triage question: sanctioned audit tuning, or an attacker disabling logging to go dark?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Disabling audit subcategories (logon, process creation, object access) blinds detection before the real attack proceeds.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security auditing shipped via Elastic Agent to logs-system.security-* (verified live).

Input.name: $username
Input.description: Interactive account that changed audit policy (SubjectUserName).

InitialAssessment.Rule: GPO-driven audit changes come from machine accounts (excluded); a human toggling audit on a server is unusual and worth confirming - disabling subcategories is more suspicious than enabling.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the interactive audit change is authorised hardening/tuning or an attempt to reduce logging before malicious activity.

Step.name: Scope the audit change and actor
Step.Purpose: Confirm actor and whether several hosts had audit changed by the same person (broad blinding).
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code == "4719" AND winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName == "$username" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, host.name, winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName, winlog.event_data.CategoryId, winlog.event_data.SubcategoryId, winlog.event_data.AuditPolicyChanges | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 30
Step.AnalystNotes: AuditPolicyChanges values indicating 'removed' (success/failure auditing turned off) for Logon or Detailed Tracking is the concerning direction. Enabling auditing is benign hardening.

Step.name: Did the actor's session then perform actions that new gaps would hide
Step.Purpose: If auditing was reduced and then privileged/logon activity occurred, the change was preparation.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND event.code IN ("4624","4672","4688","7045") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | STATS c = COUNT(*), codes = VALUES(event.code), users = VALUES(winlog.event_data.TargetUserName) | LIMIT 10
Step.AnalystNotes: Activity right after an audit reduction is what the attacker wanted unlogged; correlate the actor across both.

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows audit subcategories being DISABLED (removed) by an interactive account with no change record, especially across hosts.
INV-02 shows privileged/logon activity right after auditing was reduced by the same actor.
Node.Result: True Positive (Logging disabled before activity - IR)

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows auditing being ENABLED/hardened by a known admin, or a documented tuning change.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-AUDIT-CHANGE, INV-02-AUDIT-FOLLOWON to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: Authorised audit hardening or tuning by an administrator.

Indicators.Item: Change enables/expands auditing or matches a hardening ticket.

SOCAction.Item: Verify the change record; close as false_positive.

TruePositive.Definition: An actor disabling auditing to reduce visibility before/around malicious activity.

SOCAction.Item: Re-enable auditing (or reapply GPO); isolate the host if follow-on is present.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A misapplied local audit change diverging from GPO.

Indicators.Item: Local override that GPO will revert.

SOCAction.Item: Reapply the standard audit GPO; document.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: If subcategories were disabled: isolate and investigate the actor.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Correlate actor activity across hosts; reconstruct the reduced-visibility window.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Enforce audit policy via GPO only; alert on local overrides; restrict SeSecurityPrivilege.

QualityChecks.Check: Rule excludes machine/SYSTEM/service accounts so this is human-driven by design.
GPO refresh 4719 from machine accounts (the 4,915/30d noise) is correctly out of scope.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Audit policy restored; actor investigated; visibility gap reconstructed.
